problem: Given that $A=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 4 \\ 6 & -5\end{aligned}],$ find the product of the eigenvalues of $A.$

examples.knowledge_point: Calculating the Sum and Product of Eigenvalues of a 2x2 Matrix
examples.problem: Given that ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14069543/assets/cb48b48ef82e5d6cfe903488e80a8cbd48e286c864ba387450e01430e718d77c.png) find the sum of the eigenvalues of $A.$
examples.worked_solution:
The characteristic polynomial of $A$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}p(\lambda ) & ={\lambda }^{2}-\text{tr}(A)\lambda +\text{det}(A).\end{aligned}
$$

Now, using Vieta's formulas, we have that the roots of $p(\lambda),$ i.e., the eigenvalues of $A,$ satisfy

$$
{\begin{aligned}{\lambda }_{1}+{\lambda }_{2}=\text{tr}(A) \\ {\lambda }_{1}\cdot {\lambda }_{2}=\text{det}(A).\end{aligned}
$$

So, the sum of the eigenvalues of $A$ is equal to the trace of $A.$ 

Therefore, 

$$
\lambda_1+\lambda_2 = \textrm{tr}(A)= 9+(-6)=3.
$$
